clue.text: Ballyhoo, with contrary brood blocking entrance

indicators.note: blocking means the turned phrase stands in the way inside the publicity word

parts.note: ballyhoo is noisy publicity, which is hype

indicators.note: contrary means the words for brooding run the other way round

parts.note: to brood on eggs is to sit on them

explanation.surface: A noisy fuss about a sulking mood blocking a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway, but it is the verb, to put someone in a trance; 'contrary' and 'blocking' work on the brooding phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is literally to put them in a trance, which is what a hypnotist does.

clue.text: Fatty Arbuckle's first swim with ducks, close to shore

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the comedian's name is taken

parts.note: a swim is a dip
a duck is a score of nothing, O, so ducks are Os

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of shore

explanation.surface: The silent-film comedian Fatty Arbuckle goes swimming with ducks near the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty' looks like part of the name, but it is the definition. Os as ducks comes from cricket, where a batsman out for nought scores a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for tissue made of or storing fat.

clue.text: English queen invested in fuel for peer

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is put into a venture

parts.note: coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: An English queen puts money into fuel on behalf of a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a nobleman, but here it means an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is an equal, and coequal means of the same rank or standing.

clue.text: Assembly assuming power in recession's less than keen

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the combined letters are read from the end
assuming means taking on, so the assembly word takes the power letter inside it

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Worms
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A parliament that has taken power is lukewarm about a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assuming' puts P inside DIET to make DIPET, and 'in recession' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid support is lukewarm, showing little enthusiasm.

clue.text: Greatest shock here, as lengthy course finishing abruptly

parts.note: an epic is long, so lengthy gives epic

indicators.note: finishing abruptly means the meal-course word loses its final letter

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A long meal ends suddenly, giving the biggest shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing abruptly' cuts the last E from ENTREE, leaving ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface above an earthquake's origin, where the shaking is strongest.

clue.text: Nothing extra in schedule for layer's mate?

indicators.note: extra in means the nought is added inside the timetable word

parts.note: a roster is a duty schedule
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: No extra entries on a timetable for a bricklayer's colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' suggests someone laying bricks, but it is a hen that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is an egg-layer, and her mate is the cockerel.

clue.text: King involved in fratricide buried here, perhaps?

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside the murderer's name

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel, the first fratricide in the Bible
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king caught up in killing his brother is buried somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that a burial is only one use: many such stone heaps mark paths or summits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones, often raised over a grave as a memorial.

clue.text: Student taking tour there regularly missed out

indicators.note: regularly missed out means every other letter of these two words is dropped

explanation.surface: A student goes on a tour and some regular sessions are missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a pupil taught by a tutor, so a kind of student.

clue.text: Londoner leaving Tyneside full of himself

indicators.note: leaving means the region's letters go out of the Londoner word

parts.note: a cockney is a native East Londoner
Tyneside is in the north-east of England, NE

explanation.surface: A Londoner moves away from Tyneside, pleased with himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle, in north-east England, so it gives NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cocky is arrogantly self-confident, full of his own importance.

clue.text: Reactionary Councillor introduced to up-to-the-minute brand

indicators.note: reactionary means going backwards, so the built word is turned round
introduced to means slipped inside the word for the latest thing

parts.note: hot news is the very latest

explanation.surface: A right-wing local politician launches a trendy product line.
explanation.walkthrough: The councillor letters go after the first letter of the latest word before 'Reactionary' turns it round. 'brand' is not a trademark but a burning stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand in the old sense is a piece of burning wood carried as a light, which is a torch.

clue.text: Rook does for any number of giant duck

indicators.note: does for means stands in for, so the chess letter replaces the number letter

parts.note: giant as an adjective means immense
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook makes do with any number of enormous ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird, but it is the verb, to dunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to push them under water, which is to submerge them.

clue.text: Administrative device a ruler got wrong

indicators.note: got wrong means these letters have been put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A ruler has misunderstood a piece of bureaucratic procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator controls or administers something, whether a mechanism or a watchdog body.

clue.text: Distinguished crook now nicking cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so these three words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A notable crook now steals suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like luggage being stolen, but it is the verb saying the phrase contains the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished person is well known, famous for their achievements.

clue.text: Engaging talented nurses revolutionised plan

indicators.note: nurses means holds close, so the gifted word wraps round the turned letters

parts.note: talented means able

indicators.note: revolutionised means turned round, so the word for a plan is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention

explanation.surface: Charming, gifted nurses have transformed the hospital's plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' is the containment signal, not the hospital staff it pretends to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means pleasant and charming, and an amiable person is friendly.

clue.text: Pinky grew obsessed

parts.note: rose means went up, grew
something that ate at you obsessed you

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed Pinky became fixated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinky' looks like a nickname, but it is an adjective meaning somewhat pink.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rose-coloured, a pinkish hue.

clue.text: What crowd devised as means of getting through?

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: What a crowd invented to push its way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' only links. The question mark flags that the getting through is past a sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A password, said to a guard, lets you pass, so it is a means of getting through.

clue.text: Two pressmen given the chop

definitions.meaning: a hack and an ed (editor) are two newspaper people
chopped at roughly with blows, or dismissed

explanation.surface: Two journalists are sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits as HACK plus ED, two newspaper staff, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hacked has been cut with rough chopping blows.

clue.text: His victims might be seen taking off?

definitions.text: His victims might be seen taking off?

parts.words: His victims might be seen taking off?
parts.note: taking off suggests aircraft departing, but here it means undressing, watched by a voyeur

explanation.surface: Plane spotters watch people taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' sounds like flight, but it means taking off clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peeping Tom is a voyeur, who spies on people undressing.

clue.text: It's extremely unusual, with no money around

definitions.text: It's extremely unusual, with no money around

parts.note: O is a round nought, nothing

indicators.note: around means the nothing-money letters go round the picked ends

parts.note: pence are money

indicators.note: extremely means the two end letters of unusual are taken

explanation.surface: Great wealth is rare where there's no money about.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of riches: uncommon wherever cash is scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is lavish wealth, the opposite of having no money.

clue.text: An inch is permissible

definitions.note: in Scotland an inch is a small island

parts.note: let means allowed, permissible

explanation.surface: An inch is allowed, a matter of tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, which is the Scottish sense of an inch.

clue.text: Oriental seamen collectively on drug during festival

indicators.note: during means inside the festival word

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: on means placed on top of, in a down clue coming before

parts.note: the RN, Royal Navy, is all the sailors together
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Sailors take drugs during a holiday in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the sailors above, so before, the drug letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oriental is a person from the East, an easterner.

clue.text: Writer describing street cafe

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the pen word circles the street letters

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: An author writes about a street cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen, a Biro.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant or cafe.

clue.text: Christmas shows up heartless cleaner

indicators.note: up means read upwards, reversing in a down clue
heartless means the middle letters of the shows word are removed

parts.note: pantos, pantomimes, are traditional British Christmas shows

explanation.surface: Christmas shows show up an unfeeling cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a pantomime, a comic family show staged in Britain at Christmas. 'heartless' takes NT from PANTOS, leaving PAOS, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is a cleaning agent, a cleaner.

clue.text: Present lorry unloaded with care

parts.note: to tender is to present or offer

indicators.note: unloaded means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A truck being emptied is presented carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unloaded' leaves LY, the outside of lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something tenderly means doing it gently and with care.

clue.text: Party's policies old boy's het up about? Just so

parts.note: in US politics a party's ticket is its platform

indicators.note: het up means agitated, so these letters are stirred around

explanation.surface: An old boy gets worked up about party policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'het up' stirs BOY and O to give YBOO. Tickety-boo is dated British slang for fine or in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo is old-fashioned slang meaning all right, just as it should be.

clue.text: Question wife coming last of all in seasonal contest

indicators.note: coming last of all means the wife letter shifts to the very end

parts.note: winter is a season, giving the seasonal word
to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.surface: A wife finishes last in a winter competition and is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: WINTER VIE has its W moved by 'coming last of all' to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To interview someone is to question them formally.

clue.text: Brains from monkeys dissected by hospital

indicators.note: dissected by means cut open by, so the hospital letter goes into the rascals word

parts.note: little monkeys and tinkers are both mischievous children
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Monkey brains are cut open in a hospital laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinker is British slang for a mischievous child, as is monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Brains is informal for clever people, those who think hard.

clue.text: Finish off cold collation meant for nursery?

indicators.note: finish off means the end letter of the cold word is cut off

parts.note: a chill is a cold
a collation is a light meal, a dish

explanation.surface: Finish the cold supper meant for the children's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' cuts the last L from CHILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish things suit young children, the nursery being where they play.

clue.text: Mounted knight in ensuing charge

indicators.note: mounted means raised up, reading upwards in a down clue
in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: later means following, ensuing
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A mounted knight makes a cavalry charge in what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a cavalry attack, but it is a fee for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is the charge paid for hiring something.

clue.text: Twelve hours you could say put paid to ally

parts.note: the daylight half of the clock is loosely a day, and Fri is short for a day of the week
to end something is to put paid to it

explanation.surface: Twelve hours, so to speak, finished off a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter on your side, a companion.

clue.text: Join in dishonest practice

definitions.meaning: to join tissue or shoots together

explanation.surface: Take part in corrupt business.
explanation.definitionFit: Grafting joins plant shoots, and graft is also corruption in public office.

clue.text: Report of slow flowing river

indicators.note: report of means the word is heard spoken

parts.note: to ooze is to flow slowly

explanation.surface: An account of a sluggish river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England, the name of several in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is an English river, flowing through York among other places.
